data.content_ref: inline:SRC_003 and SRC_005 share a common underlying mechanism for nocturnal UHI: the differential rate of longwave radiative cooling between urban and rural surfaces. In SRC_003, the mechanism is the supply-side (stored heat released as longwave radiation), while in SRC_005, it is the demand-side (sky view factor controlling the efficiency of longwave loss to the cold sky). Both describe a perturbation to the same nocturnal surface energy balance term. This shared mechanism is REFUTED IF observational evidence shows that on nights with very low wind and high cloud cover, the UHI vanishes—this would imply that suppressing radiative cooling (via clouds) eliminates the differential, which would paradoxically support the shared radiative mechanism but refute the independence of the storage mechanism, as stored heat would still be present but unable to radiate. If the UHI persists under high cloud cover, the two do not share a radiative mechanism and instead depend on non-radiative processes like turbulent sensible heat or anthropogenic heat.
